guide.title: Chest Trauma
guide.lead: Chest injuries kill quickly, but several are fixable in minutes: seal an open wound, decompress a tension pneumothorax, ventilate a failing flail chest. Look, listen and feel both sides every time, and reassess often because things change fast.

sections.title: The immediate killers
rows: Absent breath sounds one side, hyperresonant, distended neck veins, low BP, hypoxia
Vented chest seal (or occlusive dressing taped on three sides)
Absent breath sounds, dull, flat neck veins, shock
Rapid transport; 1500 mL or more of blood
Muffled heart sounds, distended neck veins, low BP, equal breath sounds
Oxygen, analgesia, assist ventilation if failing

steps.title: Adults
steps.text: 4th or 5th intercostal space just in front of the mid-axillary line (or 2nd intercostal space, mid-clavicular line).

steps.title: Technique
steps.text: Over the top of the rib; listen for air; leave the catheter; reassess.

sections.title: Remember
items: Never tape or bind a flail chest
CPAP only if awake and protecting the airway; otherwise BVM
Commotio cordis: a blow to the chest causes VF – CPR and defibrillation
High-speed deceleration: think aortic injury even if stable

quiz.q: Sucking stab wound to the left chest, SpO₂ 88%. Management?
options: Vented chest seal (or three-sided occlusive dressing), oxygen, watch for tension, transport
Tape an airtight dressing on all four sides
quiz.explanation: Lift or "burp" the seal if tension develops.

quiz.q: Collapsed after a baseball hit the chest; the AED advises a shock. Cause?
options: Commotio cordis: VF from a blow at a vulnerable moment

quiz.q: A chest segment moves in on inspiration; SpO₂ 86% on a non-rebreather. Primary problem and fix?
options: Flail chest with pulmonary contusion: oxygen, analgesia, assisted ventilation if failing
quiz.explanation: The bruised lung causes the hypoxia.

quiz.q: Stab wound to the left chest: distended neck veins, BP 82/54, equal breath sounds, midline trachea:
quiz.explanation: Equal breath sounds separate it from tension.

options: 4th or 5th intercostal space just in front of the mid-axillary line

quiz.explanation: Dull percussion, flat neck veins, shock.

quiz.q: Hyperresonant chest with distended neck veins suggests:

options: 2 or more adjacent ribs broken in 2 or more places

quiz.q: Should you tape or bind a flail chest?

flashcards.question: Immediately life-threatening chest injuries
flashcards.answer: Airway obstruction, tension pneumothorax, open pneumothorax, massive hemothorax, cardiac tamponade, flail chest with pulmonary contusion.

flashcards.question: Tension pneumothorax vs massive hemothorax
flashcards.answer: Tension: hyperresonant, distended neck veins. Hemothorax: dull, flat neck veins with shock. Both: absent breath sounds.

flashcards.question: Open pneumothorax dressing
flashcards.answer: Vented chest seal; if unavailable, occlusive dressing taped on three sides. Watch for tension and lift the seal if it develops.

flashcards.question: Tension pneumothorax treatment
flashcards.answer: Clinical diagnosis. Needle decompression (ALS): adults 4th/5th intercostal space anterior to the mid-axillary line or 2nd space mid-clavicular; over the rib.

flashcards.question: Beck's triad
flashcards.answer: Hypotension, distended neck veins, muffled heart sounds: cardiac tamponade (often incomplete).

flashcards.question: Tamponade vs tension at the scene
flashcards.answer: Tamponade: equal breath sounds, midline trachea, muffled heart sounds. Tension: absent breath sounds one side, hyperresonance.

flashcards.question: Flail chest
flashcards.answer: 2 or more adjacent ribs broken in 2 or more places; paradoxical movement; contusion causes the hypoxia. Never tape or bind.

flashcards.question: Commotio cordis
flashcards.answer: VF from a blow to the chest, often young athletes. Immediate CPR and defibrillation.

critical.scenario: Stab wound to the left lateral chest: severe distress, BP 78/50, SpO₂ 82%, absent left breath sounds, hyperresonant left chest, distended neck veins, trachea shifted right.
critical.question: Diagnosis and intervention?

options.t: Left tension pneumothorax: immediate needle decompression (ALS) on the left, oxygen, emergency transport

options.f: Hyperresonance and distended veins mean air.
The injured, silent side is left.

critical.explanation: A rush of air and improving BP confirm it.

critical.scenario: Gunshot to the left parasternal chest: BP 86/58, HR 124, distended neck veins, midline trachea, equal breath sounds, very quiet heart sounds.
critical.question: Most likely injury, and the key difference from tension?

options.t: Cardiac tamponade: equal breath sounds and midline trachea rule out tension; rapid transport to cardiothoracic surgery

options.f: Neck veins are distended, not flat.

critical.explanation: Wounds in the "cardiac box" carry the highest risk.

critical.scenario: Driver hit a tree at about 80 km/h: 4-rib flail segment on the left with crackles beneath, SpO₂ 84% on a non-rebreather, RR 32 and shallow, awake. No tracheal shift; neck veins flat.
critical.question: Cause of the hypoxia, and ventilation plan?

options.t: Pulmonary contusion under the flail: positive-pressure support (BVM; CPAP only while he stays awake and protects his airway), analgesia, no binding, trauma centre

critical.explanation: The contusion worsens over hours: reassess often.
critical.kpi: Manages flail chest and pulmonary contusion with appropriate ventilation
